# Grapher v0.1.0 — Initial public preview

**Don't orchestrate agents. Compile work.**

Grapher is a local coding-agent workbench built on Pi. Use one agent for small or linear tasks; compile independent workstreams into an inspectable execution graph, execute it with a deterministic Rust runtime, and publish valid results through Git.

## Included

- **Serial workbench:** direct Pi coding tasks, graphical conversations, tool logs, provider authentication, and model settings.
- **Graph execution:** Planner/compiler workflow, user approval by default, dependency-aware parallel execution, and bounded review/rework.
- **Deterministic Rust scheduler:** explicit scheduling, bounded feedback, invalidation, persisted state, and recovery. Model outputs are not deterministic.
- **Workspace inheritance:** children inherit completed parents' filesystem state in their own workspaces, not parent conversations. The backend uses Git snapshots for inheritance and publication back to the selected project. Completion requires successful publication.

## Install from source

There are no packaged installers or standalone binaries in this preview. Follow the [quick start](https://github.com/zhexusun10/grapher#quick-start). Requirements include Node.js 22.19+, stable Rust, Git, npm, and provider authentication. Initialize the pinned Pi submodule; do not substitute a global installation.

## Platform status

| Platform | Preview status |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | Native implementation and Windows CI workflow. Requires Git for Windows Bash and host Rust build tools. Job Objects control process lifetime; workspaces are not filesystem sandboxes. |
| Linux | Native implementation and Linux CI workflow. Graph requires bubblewrap and permitted unprivileged user/mount/PID namespaces; package installation alone is insufficient. |
| macOS | Implementation uses sandbox-exec/Seatbelt. No macOS CI workflow currently exists; do not treat it as equivalently validated. |

Workflow coverage is not a blanket platform guarantee. Review the [latest CI runs](https://github.com/zhexusun10/grapher/actions) before choosing a revision.

## Known limitations and safety

- Early preview: no stable API, persisted-data compatibility, or model-quality guarantee. Back up projects and runtime data before upgrades.
- Use trusted, disposable projects first. Planning can merge changes before approval; snapshots can commit existing non-ignored changes. Reject is not rollback.
- Independent Git repositories provide version isolation, not security isolation. Source Git objects may be shared for reading; history confidentiality is not guaranteed. Shared HOME, temporary files, environment state, and external services are outside workspace inheritance.
- Model requests use your provider and may incur costs. Dependencies for node tasks are not automatically installed or propagated when ignored/untracked.
- Concurrent Runs can conflict. Preparation conflicts and publication failures may require manual intervention; failed state is retained for inspection/retry.
- Keep the local API on loopback; origin checks are not authentication.
- Fixture and scripted-local-model tests establish runtime behavior, not live-model capability or comparative benchmark performance.

See [execution semantics](https://github.com/zhexusun10/grapher/blob/main/docs/architecture/execution-model.md), [filesystem boundaries](https://github.com/zhexusun10/grapher/blob/main/docs/architecture/filesystem-isolation.md), and the [security policy](https://github.com/zhexusun10/grapher/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## Maintainer publication gate

This is a **draft prerelease**, not a stable release announcement. Before publishing: choose the intended source commit, confirm both platform CI runs on that commit, run documentation/frontend/runtime checks, review known limitations, and clearly separate offline test coverage from independently reviewed live-provider results. Do not publish while required platform checks are failing. Update the release target when further fixes are committed.
